## Design

### 2026-11-08: ![wired](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/912463b4ec3637e3f724c8ee3470beafa039680004e53265c857c9a2d28beb47.png)

**3h**

![wired](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/912463b4ec3637e3f724c8ee3470beafa039680004e53265c857c9a2d28beb47.png)
For the schematic, I decided to use a Raspberry Pi Pico W as the controller, along with an OLED screen to display the music. As you can see here, the wiring is a bit of a mess.

![cleanwire](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/379fff3db78559639f7672ab5174ffdfc477403691a69869bd1648ceacd6b984.png)
Knowing that wires can't overlap on actual PCBs, I tried to clean up the wires a bit, but only changed the design a little bit because there really wasn't much I could do.

![pcb](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/2213ce752e72d3712b01e78468b75c6349f4a2f40d5ac47353b1afe73c95c8a7.png)
I inserted the footprints and worked on the PCB. I had to remove a section of the Pico because it gave me an error for interfering with itself for some reason, but it still works. Because overlapping wires were inevitable, I resorted to using vias, which wire them on different layers so that they don't short-circuit.

### 2026-11-08: ![week5code1](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/87b51d16e54d880b21a89978d63b06115e457c6ac67b8cb3af6fa9d90ad8fdb5.png)

**3h**

![week5code1](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/87b51d16e54d880b21a89978d63b06115e457c6ac67b8cb3af6fa9d90ad8fdb5.png)
I worked on the firmware after, and this portion of the code connects the pc and Raspberry Pi through wifi since I have the W model, and it also initiates the display and defines the connection to the PC.

![week5code2](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/310df30b5a91009c0039f1a8156770dfb211e870c4f29850835996abb5ec0e25.png)
This part repeatedly checks the information coming from the PC and organizes the incoming data so it can be displayed. It prints the title of the song and artist.

![week5code3](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/db1738b219692c06842f7e67c34d4fa0e1200e54ea60b230db0c1740bcc3164f.png)
This part of the code takes the current plytime and divides it by the total length of the song, so it knows how much of the progress bar to fill. It tehn prints the progress bar, the current time, and the total time of the song.

I also had to install software and stuff on my pc for it to work.
